## Overview

This dossier draws on the 2025 [Debt Sustainability Monitor](../document-types/debt-sustainability-monitor.qmd) and the Spring 2026 [Economic Forecast](../document-types/economic-forecast.qmd), both issued by the [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) in early and mid-2026, alongside the 2026 [Country Report](../document-types/country-report.qmd) issued on 2026-06-03. The evidence characterizes the [Malta](../countries/malta.qmd) economy as robust, with real gross domestic product growth projected at 3.7% for 2026, driven by tourism and domestic consumption. Fiscal indicators show a general government deficit stabilizing around 2.2% of GDP and public debt remaining below 47% of GDP, with a projected decline to 40.8% by 2036 under a no-policy-change baseline. Key themes include persistent labor shortages, pressure on housing and infrastructure, and institutional challenges related to the justice system and transparency. Long-term fiscal sustainability assessments indicate high risk for debt stabilization due to ageing costs, requiring significant structural primary balance improvements.

## Economic

### C1\* Growth ([Growth](../parameters/growth.qmd))

#### C1-E Broken or dominated sample

[No evidence in the sources yet.]{.no-evidence}

#### C1-T Structural break in trend

- **C1-T, structural break**: Real GDP is expected to grow by 3.7% in 2026 and 3.6% in 2027. Growth is driven by domestic consumption and services. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 136" aria-label="Source: ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 136">ⓘ</button>
- **C1-T, structural break in trend**: Nominal wage growth is projected to ease from 4.2% in 2025 to 3.5% in 2026 and 2.1% in 2027. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Malta_2026-06-03, p. 3" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Malta_2026-06-03, p. 3">ⓘ</button>

#### C1-A1 Growth not thin-tailed or serially independent

[No evidence in the sources yet.]{.no-evidence}

#### C1-A2 Inherited competitiveness gap

- **C1-A2, competitiveness gap**: Labour shortages persist, particularly in tourism, healthcare, and services, despite strong employment growth. Vacancy rates continued to increase. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Malta_2026-06-03, p. 3" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Malta_2026-06-03, p. 3">ⓘ</button>

#### Other growth context

- **C1\*, context**: Real GDP grew by 4.0% in 2025 and is forecast to grow by 3.7% in 2026, driven by private and public consumption and tourism. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Malta_2026-06-03, p. 3" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Malta_2026-06-03, p. 3">ⓘ</button>
- **C1\*, context**: Employment growth is projected at 3.9% in 2025 and 3.2% in 2026, relying heavily on foreign workers. Unemployment is expected to remain low at around 3.2% in 2026. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Malta_2026-06-03, p. 3" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Malta_2026-06-03, p. 3">ⓘ</button>

## Fiscal

### C3\* Fiscal capacity and plan ([Fiscal Capacity](../parameters/fiscal-capacity.qmd))

#### C3-E Estimator fails or rests on one episode

[No evidence in the sources yet.]{.no-evidence}

#### C3-T History lags policy

- **C3-T, history lags policy**: The government deficit is forecast to remain stable at 2.2% in 2026 and fall to 2.1% in 2027. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 137" aria-label="Source: ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 137">ⓘ</button>
- **C3-T, history lags policy**: The medium-term fiscal structural plan for 2025-2028 implies an improvement of the structural primary balance of 1.4 percentage points, from -2.2% of GDP in 2025 to -0.8% in 2028. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Malta_2026-06-03, p. 4" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Malta_2026-06-03, p. 4">ⓘ</button>

#### C3-A Default is chosen, not only suffered

- **C3-A, default is chosen, not only suffered**: The tax system faces challenges regarding aggressive tax planning risks, with features creating opportunities for double non-taxation and profit shifting. [Malta](../countries/malta.qmd) does not publish tax expenditure reporting. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Malta_2026-06-03, p. 4, 10, 39" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Malta_2026-06-03, p. 4, 10, 39">ⓘ</button>

#### Other fiscal context

- **C3\*, context**: The structural primary balance is projected at -1.0% of GDP on average for 2026-2035. The fiscal consolidation space is 50% in the baseline scenario. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 41, 42" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 41, 42">ⓘ</button>
- **C3\*, context**: The European Commission projects a structural primary deficit of 1% of GDP as of 2026. This is in line with past fiscal performance. Ageing-related expenditure is projected to decrease slightly over the medium term but increase over the long term. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 207" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 207">ⓘ</button>
- **C3\*, context**: The S2 indicator points to high risk, requiring an 8.1 percentage point improvement, driven by ageing costs (6.5 pps). The S1 indicator points to medium risk, requiring a 3.1 percentage point effort. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 208" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 208">ⓘ</button>
- **C3\*, context**: The government deficit fell to 2.2% of GDP in 2025 and is projected to remain stable in 2026, reflecting strong revenue growth offsetting increased expenditure on wages and energy subsidies. It is projected to fall to 2.1% in 2027. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Malta_2026-06-03, p. 3-4" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Malta_2026-06-03, p. 3-4">ⓘ</button>
- **C3\*, context**: Public debt is expected to stabilize at around 46% of GDP by 2027. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Malta_2026-06-03, p. 4" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Malta_2026-06-03, p. 4">ⓘ</button>
- **C3\*, context**: Total tax revenues amounted to 28.9% of GDP in 2024, well below the EU average of 39.4%. Corporate income tax accounts for a large share of revenues. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Malta_2026-06-03, p. 10-11" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Malta_2026-06-03, p. 10-11">ⓘ</button>
- **C3\*, context**: Ageing-related spending is projected to rise by 9 percentage points of GDP between 2025 and 2070, driven by pensions, healthcare, and long-term care. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Malta_2026-06-03, p. 36" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Malta_2026-06-03, p. 36">ⓘ</button>

## Market Signals

- **Factor decoupling**: Business confidence and investment indicators show mixed results, with high administrative burdens and regulatory barriers cited by firms. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Malta_2026-06-03, p. 13, 48-49" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Malta_2026-06-03, p. 13, 48-49">ⓘ</button>
- **Rollover pessimism**: The 10-year sovereign yield spread vs. German Bund is 91 basis points as of 31 December 2025. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 209" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 209">ⓘ</button>

## Outlook Material

- **Outlook Factors, rule of law**: Concerns persist over the efficiency of the justice system. The time to resolve civil and commercial cases increased from 432 to 491 days between 2016 and 2024. Resources for the judiciary are limited, with a low number of judges per capita. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Malta_2026-06-03, p. 11-12, 64" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Malta_2026-06-03, p. 11-12, 64">ⓘ</button>
- **Outlook Factors, rule of law**: Transparency issues exist in public procurement and lobbying. Ministers stopped publicly declaring family income after 2023. No comprehensive rules on lobbying or robust asset declaration requirements are in place. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Malta_2026-06-03, p. 13-14, 64" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Malta_2026-06-03, p. 13-14, 64">ⓘ</button>
- **Housing and Infrastructure**: Rapid population growth (34% increase between 2015 and 2025) has put strain on infrastructure, land use, and public services. Housing costs are a significant driver of poverty, with 7.7% of those at risk of poverty having mortgage or rent arrears in 2025. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Malta_2026-06-03, p. 5, 97-101" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Malta_2026-06-03, p. 5, 97-101">ⓘ</button>
- **Energy Security and Climate**: [Malta](../countries/malta.qmd) is highly vulnerable to climate risks. The energy mix is skewed towards imported fossil fuels. Renewable energy share in electricity mix was 16.7% in 2025, below the EU average of 45%. Fossil fuel subsidies accounted for 1% of GDP in 2024. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Malta_2026-06-03, p. 5, 15-17, 75" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Malta_2026-06-03, p. 5, 15-17, 75">ⓘ</button>
- **Labor Market and Skills**: Severe skills shortages exist, particularly in STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics) and green transition sectors. Participation in STEM post-secondary education is significantly below the EU average (13.8% vs 25.2%). <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Malta_2026-06-03, p. 19-20, 92" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Malta_2026-06-03, p. 19-20, 92">ⓘ</button>
- **Social Protection**: Social transfers reduced the monetary poverty rate by only 24.9% in 2025, below the EU average of 33.2%. Vulnerable groups, including third-country nationals and persons with disabilities, face higher risks of poverty and exclusion. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Malta_2026-06-03, p. 21-22, 88" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Malta_2026-06-03, p. 21-22, 88">ⓘ</button>
